title: RSL Companion consolidated account export
description: Payload POSTed to {ApiBaseUrl}/api/sync/consolidated/raw. One complete snapshot of one game account; a full replace, not a delta. Self-identifying: the server routes by the in-game accountId it carries. Since schema 13 this is the ONLY payload the uploader sends — the separate clan export was withdrawn. Human-readable contract and changelog: export-schema.md (keep both in sync, same commit).

x-relatedCatalogs.roles: role-names.json — champions[].roleId to role name. Static game metadata (the HeroRole enum), shipped here because roleId is an opaque int without it.
x-relatedCatalogs.artifacts: artifact-enums.json — artifacts[]/accessories[] kindId (slot), statKindId, rankId and setKindId to names. Static game metadata (the ArtifactKindId / StatKindId / ArtifactRankId / ArtifactSetKindId enums).
x-relatedCatalogs.heroBaseStats: hero_base_stats.json — every champion ASCENSION VARIANT's stored base stats plus the client's growth coefficients, the catalog champions[].baseStats is computed from. Bundled with the uploader (extraction/exports/) rather than here because it is 2.2 MB; a consumer needs it only for champions the player does NOT own, since an owned copy's numbers arrive on this payload already resolved. Produced by RslCompanionMetadata; contract in its docs/hero-base-stats-findings.md.
x-relatedCatalogs.relics: relic-enums.json — relics[].sockets[].shapeKindId to socket shape. Relic and gemstone typeId are NOT named there: they are a catalog of the game (name, rarity, group, skill, stat bonuses) and belong in a champion-metadata-style catalog keyed on typeId.

accountId.description: In-game account id. The routing key; always equals account.accountId.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the snapshot was taken.

uploaderVersion.description: Desktop app build that produced this payload. Stamped by the app, NOT by the extraction engine, so it is absent from engine-level dumps.

gameVersion.description: Live Raid build the snapshot was read from — the build the export RAN AGAINST. Null when it could not be determined. NOT the provenance of champions[].baseStats; see baseStatsCatalog.

baseStatsCatalog.description: Which cut of the champion base-stat catalog produced every champions[].baseStats block in this payload. Top level rather than per hero because one export uses exactly one catalog. ABSENT when no catalog was loaded — in which case no hero carries baseStats either. THIS IS NOT gameVersion, and the two come apart in the ordinary case: gameVersion is the build the export ran against, this is the build the numbers were computed from, and a user who updates Raid before a refreshed catalog ships exports with the new gameVersion and stats from the old catalog. CONSUMER RULE: a baseStats block whose catalog gameVersion trails the payload's gameVersion is SUSPECT, NOT WRONG — most rebalances touch few champions — so flag it for re-sync, never discard it. Without this field a stale computed block is indistinguishable from a fresh one, which matters because a rebalance silently invalidates every block already stored server-side until each user re-exports.

generatedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the producer generated the catalog. The catalog's version identity — compare these to tell two cuts apart.

gameVersion.description: Game build the CATALOG was cut from. Null when the catalog does not state one. Compare against the payload's top-level gameVersion, not against it as an equal.

accountId.description: Duplicate of the top-level accountId; always equal.

resources.description: ALWAYS the complete allowlist (49 ids as of schema 3). Ids the account holds none of are present with quantity 0, so a missing id means the allowlist changed - never 'zero owned'. Join on id, NEVER on name: names track in-game renames (three changed in v1.5.4). NEVER ALL-ZERO: because every id is emitted unconditionally, a failed read returns a full-length array of zeroes rather than an empty one - so length proves nothing here and the `contains` constraint above is the real check. Every account holds at least some Silver, so at least one quantity is always non-zero. The uploader refuses to send an all-zero array; a consumer seeing one should discard the payload and keep what it has, never apply it (applying it zeroes the account's entire inventory).

id.description: Stable allowlist id. The only safe join key.

name.description: Display label. NOT stable across releases.

x-soulEconomy.description: Corrected in schema 3 / v1.5.4. Ids 10101, 10102, 10104, 10105, 10201 and 10204 are a DEFUNCT earlier soul system: they are not allowlisted, are never emitted, and must not be mapped onto the ids below - doing so is the bug v1.5.4 fixed.

ids.1111: Mortal Soul Coin (was 'Silver Soul Coin'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.1112: Immortal Soul Coin (was 'Gold Soul Coin'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.1113: Eternal Soul Coin (was 'Immortal Essence'; value was wrong before v1.5.4)
ids.10205: Eternal Essence (legacy; still emitted, semantics unverified)

champions.description: The owned champion roster. RENAMED from `heroes` in schema 16, and THE ONLY NAME since schema 17, which removed the alias. A consumer that also reads older payloads uses `champions ?? heroes`; that fallback must outlive this removal by a wide margin, because the uploader is installed on user machines and updates opt-in, so pre-v1.14 installs keep sending `heroes` alone for as long as they run. NEVER EMPTY: the game gives every new player a starter champion, so there is no such thing as an account with zero. A zero-length array is therefore a failed read, not an empty roster — the uploader refuses to send one, and this constraint makes a consumer reject it rather than faithfully applying it and wiping the account's champions. Treat a validation failure here as 'discard this payload and keep what you have'.

name.description: Null when the champion index cannot resolve it.

instanceId.description: int64. Unique per OWNED COPY. Join key for factionGuardians and artifacts.

baseTypeId.description: Champion type, ascension digit stripped. Copies of one champion share this.

factionId.description: 0 when unresolved. Same id space as factionGuardians[].factionId.

roleId.description: Champion role: 0 Attack, 1 Defense, 2 Health (shown as 'HP'), 3 Support, 4 Evolve, 5 Xp. NULL — never 0 — when unresolved, because 0 is a real role. Static per champion, NOT per copy: it is the game's HeroRole enum on the shared champion type, so every copy of a champion reports the same value and the id table is game metadata (role-names.json), not account data. Null on roughly a fifth of a mature roster because the client hydrates a champion's type lazily; prefer a champion metadata catalog keyed on baseTypeId as the authoritative source, and treat this field as a convenience copy.

elementId.description: This copy's AFFINITY (the game calls it Element), off HeroForm.Element. Raw id, deliberately unnamed here for the same reason forms[].element is raw in the champion index: the frontend renders affinity from icons keyed by the id, so a name table would be one more thing to keep in sync. NULL MEANS UNKNOWN, NOT 'no affinity' — every champion has one, but the client hydrates a champion's shared type lazily, so a copy the player has never rendered has nothing to read it from; the exporter backfills from another copy of the same baseTypeId (affinity is champion-constant) before giving up. Consumers need it to select a champion's row out of affinityBonuses[].

statBreakdown.description: The game's own TOTAL STATS table for this copy: per stat, the total plus one entry per contributing source. Keys are StatKindId AS STRINGS, same as baseStats. AN ABSENT SOURCE MEANS 'CONTRIBUTES NOTHING', NEVER ZERO — the client itself distinguishes the two (every cell carries a _hasValue flag) and draws a blank cell rather than a 0. Which columns this producer actually computed is stated by top-level statBreakdownSources, and a source missing from THAT list is 'not modelled yet', which is a different thing again; a consumer must render neither as a real zero. Absent on a champion whose baseStats could not be computed, since there is then no base for a percentage to apply to.

isPercentage.description: True for the stats the game shows as percentages (C.RATE, C.DMG, C.HEAL, IGN.DEF). For these a non-absolute bonus is PERCENTAGE POINTS, not a fraction of the base: 15% base + 37% from artifacts shows as 57%, not 21%.

total.description: The number on the game's screen. Rounded as the client rounds — once per column, half to even — so it is not always the sum a consumer would compute from the sources by another rule.

sources.description: source name -> rounded contribution. Names match statBreakdownSources exactly.

baseStats.description: This copy's BASIC STATS — the game's own name for the first column of its Total Stats breakdown, i.e. the numbers before any gear, Great Hall, arena, mastery, guardian, empowerment, blessing, relic or area bonus. Keys are the game's StatKindId AS STRINGS, the same ids artifacts[].primaryBonus.statKindId uses (1 Health, 2 Attack, 3 Defence, 4 Speed, 5 Resistance, 6 Accuracy, 7 CriticalChance, 8 CriticalDamage, 9 CriticalHeal, 10 IgnoreDefence) — no translation table needed. THIS IS WHAT A PERCENTAGE ARTIFACT BONUS IS A PERCENTAGE OF: a bonus with isAbsolute=false carries a FRACTION (0.18 = +18%), and without these numbers there is nothing to take 18% of. Percentage bonuses are percentages of these values and are ADDED, never compounded off each other. NOT CHAMPION-CONSTANT, unlike roleId: it is derived from this copy's ascension, stars and level, so a consumer CANNOT recover it from a champion catalog keyed on baseTypeId and should prefer this rather than treating it as a fallback. ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN — never coalesce to 0. Omitted entirely when level or stars could not be read, when level exceeds its rank's cap, or when the catalog predates the champion; an individual stat kind missing from the catalog entry is likewise absent. A 0 that IS present is a real zero: base Accuracy is genuinely 0 on 6,806 of 7,166 champion variants, while base Resistance is never below 30.

blessingId.description: Equipped blessing, as the game's BlessingType id; 0 = none. Only ever non-zero when awakeningLevel > 0. Replaced the blessingChosen boolean, which reported the Nullable hasValue flag as if it were the id.

isFactionGuardian.description: This copy is placed in an Academy guardian slot.

skills.description: This copy's skills and how far each is upgraded, sorted by typeId. Always present; empty only on a failed read (every champion has at least one skill). Since schema 20 each entry also says which of the champion's FORMS it belongs to. Per-skill metadata - name, description, cooldown, and the MAXIMUM level - is intentionally absent: it is constant game data, joined on typeId from a skill catalog. Without that catalog 'level 5' cannot be read as maxed or not.

typeId.description: Skill type id, and the catalog join key. TREAT AS OPAQUE - join it, do not derive it. It is usually baseTypeId*10 + slot (Kael, base 1510 -> 15101..15104) and is stable across copies and ascensions, but two documented exceptions break any derivation: a champion with a second form ALSO carries that form's block at 800000 + the own-block id (10 champions, 53 skills on the mapping account, which is why skills[] can hold 10-12 entries), and a skill can belong to another champion's id block entirely (Ezio Auditore and Edward Kenway both carry 102505). Slots are also not dense: a 3-skill champion may report 15101/15103/15104.

level.description: Upgrade level, 1-BASED. 1 means un-upgraded, so books applied = level-1. Observed range 1-9; the cap is per-skill and lives in the catalog, not here.

formIndex.description: Which of the champion's forms this skill is on: 0 the base form, 1 a transformation's second form, matching forms[].index in champion_index.json. ABSENT, NEVER 0, when unresolved - 0 is the base form, a real answer, so the field has no spare sentinel; group with `?? 'unknown'`, not with `?? 0`. Resolved by the producer against the copy's OWN ascension variant of the champion, which is why it is here and not left to a catalog join: attributing a skill consumer-side means honouring the per-skill ascension span in forms[].skills[], because ascension REPLACES skills on 336 of 1,034 playable champions and both halves of a swapped pair sit in the same form list.

masteries.description: Always present and fully populated - deliberately verbose so consumers never null-check. Per-node metadata (name/tree/tier/cost) is intentionally absent: it is constant game data, joined from mastery_index.json in the RslCompanionMetadata repo.

selected.description: Chosen mastery node ids; empty array when none, never null. The id encodes position: 500*tree*tier*slot, tier being the tens digit.

totalScrolls.description: Unspent PLUS already spent on selected (each node's activation cost).

statBreakdownSources.description: Which statBreakdown sources THIS PRODUCER modelled, in the game's own column order. It exists because a per-champion breakdown cannot express the difference between 'this source contributes nothing to this champion' and 'this producer does not compute this source yet' — both look like an absent key, and only one of them may be drawn as a zero. The game's full set is basic, artifacts, greatHall, arena, masteries, factionGuardians, empowerment, blessing, relic. AREA BONUSES WILL NEVER APPEAR HERE: they depend on a location the player picks from a dropdown, so there is no single per-champion number — they are published at account level as areaBonuses[] instead. Absent when no champion carries a statBreakdown.

affinityBonuses.description: The Great Hall's AFFINITY BONUSES tab, as account data: what this account has bought, per affinity and stat. The same table feeds every champion of that affinity, which is why it is here once rather than repeated per champion — join it on champions[].elementId. THE WHOLE GRID THE GAME DECLARES IS SENT — four affinities x six stat tracks, 24 entries — so a track the account has not bought is present with level 0, not missing. That makes the payload self-describing: a consumer can draw the screen without hardcoding the axes, and a track Plarium adds appears on its own. A pair genuinely ABSENT means the game has no such track (C.RATE is the standing example). An ABSENT ARRAY means the table could not be read, which is NOT the same as an account that has bought nothing.

elementId.description: Affinity, the same raw id space champions[].elementId uses.

statKindId.description: Stat, the same id space baseStats and the artifact bonuses use. Six tracks here: 1 HP, 2 ATK, 3 DEF, 5 RES, 6 ACC, 8 C.DMG. C.RATE (7) is genuinely absent — the Great Hall has no Critical Rate track.

level.description: 1-based as the game displays it ('3/10'), and 0 for a track this account has not bought — a real, known state, not a missing read. Carried alongside value because neither derives the other without the static per-level table, which stays in the client and is not on the wire.

value.description: What this level is worth: a flat amount when isAbsolute, else a fraction of the champion's Basic Stat (0.2 = +20%). 0 at level 0, where the game grants nothing.

isAbsolute.description: NOT CONSTANT ACROSS THE TABLE. HP, ATK, DEF and C.DMG are fractions of the Basic Stat; RESISTANCE AND ACCURACY ARE FLAT (+5 to +80). Assuming percentages throughout computes baseResistance x 80 where the game adds 80.

areaBonuses.description: The Great Hall's AREA BONUSES tab (internally the Observatory), as account data: what this account has bought, per location and stat. A SEPARATE TABLE from affinityBonuses, not the same one keyed differently — it covers Speed (4) and Ignore Defence (10) on top of the other six, and its per-level curve is linear where the affinity one steps unevenly. EVERY LOCATION OFFERS THE SAME EIGHT TRACKS, so the grid is a uniform 13 x 8 = 104 entries on game build 11.71.0, all of them sent, unbought ones at level 0. It is also the one bonus table that is not a per-champion column: the game's Total Stats overlay picks one location from a dropdown, so a single number per champion would be meaningless.

locationId.description: Location, a raw id (1-13 on game build 11.71.0, in three tiers: 1+8, 2-5+9+10, 6+7+11-13; the tiers currently carry identical values and are not on the wire). Raw for the same reason elementId is: the consumer keys its own labels off the id. Do not hardcode the range — the array carries every location the client declares.

statKindId.description: Stat, the same id space as everywhere else. Eight tracks here: 1 HP, 2 ATK, 3 DEF, 4 SPD, 5 RES, 6 ACC, 8 C.DMG, 10 IGN.DEF.

level.description: 1-based as displayed, and 0 for an unbought track. Every declared (location, stat) pair is sent, so 0 appears rather than the pair being omitted.

value.description: Flat amount when isAbsolute, else a fraction of the Basic Stat.

isAbsolute.description: SPEED, RESISTANCE AND ACCURACY ARE FLAT here (+2 to +20 and +8 to +80); HP, ATK, DEF, C.DMG and IGN.DEF are fractions.

factionGuardians.description: Academy guardian slots. Each slot fuses up to TWO copies of one champion, hence the First/Second pair.

heroTypeId.description: Champion type WITH the ascension digit (366 = base 360 at ascension 6). Do NOT join this onto champions[].baseTypeId.

heroBaseTypeId.description: Ascension stripped. THIS is what joins to champions[].baseTypeId. The game's own field is misleadingly named HeroBaseTypeId but carries the ascension digit; both forms are published so consumers need not guess.

firstHeroInstanceId.description: Null when that half of the slot is empty.

secondHeroInstanceId.description: Null when that half of the slot is empty.

artifacts.description: GEAR the account owns - helmet, chest, gloves, boots, weapon, shield (kindId 1-6) - equipped AND vaulted, with real stats. Rings/cloaks/banners are NOT here; they are in accessories[]. BREAKING CHANGE IN SCHEMA 9: through schema 8 this array was the equipped-artifact MAP across all nine slots with every stat field hard-zero, and consumers were told a 0 meant 'unknown'. Both of those are now false - the array is an OWNED list (2851 gear on the reference account, 1963 of them unequipped), accessories have moved out, and a 0 is a real 0. Three migration traps: reading this array for accessories now silently finds none; array length is an owned count, not an equipped count (test equippedByHeroId != null for that); and code that gates writes on 'stat != 0' will now drop legitimate zeroes. RECONCILING WITH THE GAME: length equals the in-game gear total exactly, and the count with equippedByHeroId == null equals the in-game unequipped total exactly - measured live 2026-08-02 at 2851 / 1963. Those are a SNAPSHOT, not constants - they move whenever the player farms, sells or equips (the same account eight hours earlier gave 2811 / 1922). What holds is the relationship, tested against counters read at the same moment. The one category still absent is the MAILBOX: unclaimed items belong to no inventory until collected and are counted in neither this array nor the in-game counter it reconciles against. May legitimately be empty on a brand-new account.

accessories.description: Rings, cloaks and banners (kindId 7-9) the account owns, equipped AND vaulted. Identical record shape to artifacts[]; new in schema 9, where these records were previously mixed into artifacts[] as ids without stats. Kept separate because the game keeps them separate (their own inventory and their own counter), because a consumer rarely needs gear and accessories in the same request, and so the server can store and serve the two independently. Note accessories are faction-locked: requiredFactionId is non-zero on all of them (2969 of 2969 on the reference account), where gear is unrestricted. Reconciles exactly against the in-game accessory counters - measured live 2026-08-02: 2969 total, 2000 with equippedByHeroId == null. Those numbers are a snapshot of one account at one moment, not constants - see the note on artifacts[].

relics.description: Every RELIC the account owns, equipped AND in storage, each with its gemstone sockets. New in schema 11; nothing resembling it existed before, so there is no migration - a consumer that ignores the array is exactly as correct as it was in schema 10. Its own array rather than part of artifacts[] because relics are a separate inventory in game, with their own counters, their own id space and their own upgrade currencies (Basalt and Starstone, both new resource ids in this schema). RECONCILING WITH THE GAME: length equals the in-game relic total and the count with equippedByHeroId == null equals the in-game unequipped total - measured live 2026-08-03 at 377 total / 240 unequipped / 137 equipped. A SNAPSHOT, not constants: check the relationship against counters read at the same moment, never the literals. One relic per champion is what this account shows (137 relics across 137 champions, none with two), but that is an observation about the game's current rules, not a guarantee the payload enforces - the field is a per-relic hero reference, so handle a hero appearing twice.

gemstones.description: Every GEMSTONE the account owns, socketed AND in storage. The game class is RelicStone; the UI calls them gemstones. Separate from relics[] for the reason accessories[] is separate from artifacts[]: the game counts them as their own inventory, and MOST OF THEM ARE IN NO RELIC AT ALL - 303 of 543 on the reference account. Nesting them under the relic holding them would have hidden 56% of the inventory, which is the same shape of loss that made schema 8's equipped-only artifacts[] look plausible while missing two thirds of the data. Joins to relics[] both ways: a socket's stoneId is a gemstones[].id, and that gemstone's socketedInRelicId points back at the relic. Measured live 2026-08-03: 543 total, 240 socketed, 303 free; both directions of the join agreed on all 240 with no dangling reference.

clanId.description: int64 id of the clan this account belongs to (the game calls a clan an Alliance). Null when the account is in no clan AND when the value could not be validated — this payload cannot distinguish the two, so never infer 'left the clan' from null. Stable and usable as a join key on its own: two accounts in the same clan report the same clanId, which is how clan membership is built: from each member importing their own account. The member ROSTER is not emitted and will not be — it describes clanmates who never used RSL Companion. That is a consent decision, not a cost one.

clanName.description: The clan's display name, as the game shows it. Null when the account is in no clan, and also when the name could not be read on this run — treat null as 'this export says nothing about the name', never as 'the clan has no name', and never overwrite a known name with it. New in schema 14; every export before that omitted the field entirely, so an absent key and a null mean the same thing to a consumer. Join on clanId, never on this: names are not unique and can be changed by the clan's leader at any time.

arenaTeam.description: NEW IN SCHEMA 19. Classic Arena's one saved attack team. Null when the account has no saved team, and also when the value could not be validated this run — the same accepted ambiguity clanId already has; never infer 'the team was cleared' from null. Carries a STAT SNAPSHOT taken when last saved/used (see teamInfo), which can be stale against champions[] — join heroes[].inventoryHeroId onto champions[].instanceId for current numbers. See 'What is not here' below: no PvE stage mode (Dungeons, Doom Tower, Cursed City, Faction Wars, Event Dungeon, Foggy Forest) has a saved team AT ALL, by the game's own design — this is not an incomplete read, there is nothing to read for those modes.

arena3v3Teams.description: NEW IN SCHEMA 19. Tag Team (3v3) Arena's saved defense/attack slots — normally 3, but treat as 'however many the account has set,' not a fixed length. ABSENT (the key is missing) means the read could not be validated this run — an offset drifted, or the branch wasn't attached — the same rule affinityBonuses[]/areaBonuses[] use, for the same reason: an empty array would make a failed read indistinguishable from an account that genuinely has none set. A PRESENT array, even empty, means it was read successfully.

siegePresets.description: NEW IN SCHEMA 19. Siege's per-map-slot presets — normally 4, treat as 'however many the account has set.' Simpler than teamInfo: bare hero ids, NO stat snapshot, because Siege reads the live roster at attack time rather than freezing one at save time. Same absent-vs-empty rule as arena3v3Teams[].

teamInfo.description: One saved team (the game's TeamSetup). Backs both arenaTeam and arena3v3Teams[] items.

combatPower.description: The team's combined power as the game computed it when last saved/used.

leaderSlotIndex.description: Which heroes[] entry (by array position, not by slot number) is the team leader.

heroes.description: The team's roster. Usually 4, but not schema-constrained to be — read the array length rather than assuming it.

teamSlotHero.description: One hero as FROZEN INTO a saved team (the game's HeroSlotSetup) — a snapshot taken when the team was last saved/used, not a live join. grade/level/empowerLevel can be stale versus the account's current champions[] entry for the same hero.

heroTypeId.description: The champion template — NOT the join key for this account's roster. Champion metadata (name, faction, role) comes from a champion catalog keyed on this, same as elsewhere on this payload.

inventoryHeroId.description: This account's specific hero instance. THE join key onto champions[].instanceId for this hero's current (non-snapshotted) data.

slot.description: The team-formation slot this hero occupies (distinct from its position in the heroes[] array).

grade.description: Star rank AS OF the snapshot. May differ from the champion's current grade in champions[].

empowerLevel.description: Empower (skin-tier stat boost) level AS OF the snapshot.

siegePreset.description: One Siege map-slot preset (the game's UserSiegePresetInfo). No stat snapshot, unlike teamInfo — Siege reads the live roster at attack time.

slot.description: 0-based LIST ORDER, not a map-stable slot identifier — do not assume it survives the player rearranging presets.

heroIds.description: Bare inventoryHeroId values (join onto champions[].instanceId) — no stat snapshot.

artifact.description: One owned artifact. The same shape backs artifacts[] (gear) and accessories[]; kindId decides which array it lands in. Every field is read from the game's own record, so a 0 is a real 0 - unlike schemas 7-8, nothing here is a placeholder.

artifactId.description: Instance id, unique across BOTH arrays, and stable for the life of the piece (it survives upgrades and re-equips) - so it is the join key for change detection.

kindId.description: Slot, from the game's ArtifactKindId enum: 1 Helmet, 2 Chest, 3 Gloves, 4 Boots, 5 Weapon, 6 Shield, 7 Ring, 8 Cloak (the UI calls it Amulet), 9 Banner. WARNING: schemas 7-8 documented a DIFFERENT and incorrect order (1 Weapon, 2 Helmet, 3 Shield, 4 Gauntlets, 5 Chestplate); a consumer that hard-coded those labels is mislabelling slots. The order above is the enum's own, corroborated by which primary stat each slot always rolls. Names: artifact-enums.json.

setKindId.description: TWO ID SPACES IN ONE FIELD. 0-66 are artifact SETS, where 0 means NO SET - a real value, not 'unknown'. 1000-1004 are ACCESSORY EFFECTS: one item's own effect, with no piece count and no set bonus, occurring on ~2.6% of accessories and on no gear. Grouping 'by set' across the 1000s invents five sets that do not exist. Join on the id, never the name - Cleansing, Bloodshield, Reaction and Revenge occur in both spaces. Both tables: artifact-enums.json (`sets` and `accessoryEffects`). The set names published before 2026-08-02 were wrong from id 4 onward; re-derive any stored labels.

level.description: Upgrade level. 0 is a real, common value (an un-upgraded drop).

ascendLevel.description: Ascension level. ascendBonus is non-null exactly when this is > 0.

requiredFactionId.description: Faction the piece is locked to; 0 = unrestricted. Same id space as champions[].factionId. Non-zero on every accessory, zero on gear.

equippedByHeroId.description: int64. The hero instance id wearing this piece, joining to champions[].instanceId - or NULL when it sits in the vault, which is the majority of records. Null means 'not equipped', never 'wearer unknown'. This replaces schema 8's heroInstanceId, which was non-null on every record because only equipped artifacts were exported.

price.description: Silver cost of the next upgrade.

failedUpgrades.description: Failed upgrade attempts since the last success - the game's pity counter.

revision.description: Server-side revision of this record, bumped when the game changes it. Lets a sync diff instead of rewriting the whole vault.

primaryBonus.description: Always present. Replaces schema 8's primaryStatId, which was always 0 and carried no value alongside it.

ascendBonus.description: The bonus granted by ascension; null unless ascendLevel > 0.

relic.description: One owned relic. ACCOUNT STATE ONLY: a relic's name, rarity, group, skill and stat bonuses live on the shared RelicType, which is a catalog of the game rather than anything about this player - the same split that keeps skill names and mastery-node metadata out of champions[]. Join those on typeId.

id.description: Instance id, unique within the account and stable across upgrades and re-equips - the join key for change detection, and what a socket's stoneId is NOT (that is a gemstone id, a different space).

typeId.description: The shared RelicType this is a copy of; the join key into a relic catalog. Opaque - 57 distinct values in range 1-86 on the reference account. NOT named in relic-enums.json: the game ships l10n:relic/name?id=N keys but this client build has no localized strings behind them and falls back to placeholder text ('Relic 12 name'), so no honest name table can be built from memory today. Gemstone type names DO resolve.

rank.description: 1-5 observed. Raising a relic from rank N to N+1 is paid for in Rank N Basalt, resource id 19000+N - which is why there are exactly five Basalt ranks. Rank 6 exists as an upgrade target ('Used to upgrade a Rank 5 Relic to Rank 6') but no rank-6 relic occurred on the reference account, so the upper bound is deliberately not constrained here.

level.description: Upgrade level, paid for in Starstone (resource id 4000). Observed 0, 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 - it steps by 3, and 0 is a real and common value (213 of 377). Do not assume every integer in the range occurs.

equippedByHeroId.description: int64. Hero instance id wearing this relic, joining to champions[].instanceId - or NULL when it is in storage, which is most of them. Null means 'not equipped', never 'wearer unknown'.

sockets.description: The relic's gemstone sockets in the game's own order. 1-4 per relic (170/149/55/3 on the reference account). Count and shapes are fixed by the relic's type; what varies per copy is which are filled.

relicSocket.description: One gemstone socket. A gemstone only fits a socket of its own shape, so shapeKindId is what decides what can go in.

shapeKindId.description: Socket shape, the game's RelicStoneShapeKindId enum. Names in relic-enums.json - but read the provenance note there before using them: the enum's five members are Circle, Triangle, Square, Diamond, Pentagon and the observed values are exactly 1-5, yet the member-to-value binding is inferred from DECLARATION ORDER and is not independently confirmed. Treat the id as authoritative and the label as provisional.

stoneId.description: The gemstones[].id socketed here, or NULL when the socket is empty. Null is the common case (405 of 645 sockets). This is a gemstone instance id and does NOT join to relics[].id.

gemstone.description: One owned gemstone (game class RelicStone). ACCOUNT STATE ONLY, same split as relics[]: name, rarity, shape and skill hang off the shared RelicStoneType and are joined on typeId.

id.description: Instance id - what relics[].sockets[].stoneId points at.

typeId.description: The shared RelicStoneType; the join key into a gemstone catalog. 68 distinct values on the reference account. Unlike relic type names, these DO resolve from the game's l10n table (l10n:relic-stone/name?id=N, 120 ids) - they are still catalog data and so are not shipped in the payload.

socketedInRelicId.description: The relics[].id this gemstone sits in, or NULL when it is in storage. Derived by inverting the sockets, so it is exactly consistent with them by construction - it is a convenience for consumers that index gemstones directly, not a second source of truth.

artifactBonus.description: One stat line. isAbsolute decides how value reads: true = a flat amount (+120 ATK), false = a FRACTION of the champion's base stat (0.18 = +18%, NOT 0.18%). The value comes from the game's Q32.32 fixed-point storage divided by 2^32 and rounded to 6 decimals, so a relative value may exceed 1.0 (1.0 = +100% on an ascended piece) - do not validate it as a 0-1 probability. WARNING for consumers holding older data: schemas 9-11 used a 2^31 divisor and so emitted EVERY value here at exactly double the game's - a 6-star +16 speed boot reported 90 against a real cap of 45. Fixed in schema 12. Nothing on the record distinguishes a doubled row from a corrected one, so affected accounts must be re-synced rather than halved in place; a stored main stat above the game's 6-star +16 table (SPD 45, HP 4080, ATK/DEF 265, ACC/RES 96, HP%/ATK%/DEF%/C.RATE 0.6, C.DMG 0.8, banner HP 6120 and ATK/DEF 398) is doubled data. GLYPHS: powerUpValue is a SEPARATE ADDEND to value, never folded into it - a consumer summing gear must add both, and one that ignores it under-reports every glyphed champion. This description previously claimed _powerUpValue was 'the upgrade screen's preview of the next roll, null on every record'; that was wrong, and the evidence for it was one account that had glyphed nothing. Diffed against the game's own Total Stats screen on a glyphed champion, the amounts missing from a gear total were exactly these values, on every stat at once. Still NOT exported: _rarityBasedPowerUpValue, which read 0 on every line of a glyphed account including the glyphed ones, so nothing is known about what it means.

statKindId.description: Game enum StatKindId: 1 Health, 2 Attack, 3 Defence, 4 Speed, 5 Resistance, 6 Accuracy, 7 CriticalChance, 8 CriticalDamage, 9 CriticalHeal, 10 IgnoreDefence. Only 1-8 occur on artifacts. Names: artifact-enums.json.

value.description: Flat amount when isAbsolute, otherwise a fraction (0.18 = 18%).

level.description: How many times this substat has been rolled up. 0 is a real value (never upgraded), not 'missing'.

powerUpValue.description: The GLYPH on this stat line (the game's 'Power Up'), 0 when there is none. Same Q32.32 scaling as value, and it inherits this line's isAbsolute - a glyph upgrades the substat it sits on, so a flat HP line gets flat HP and an HP% line gets percentage points. A SEPARATE ADDEND: this line's contribution is value + powerUpValue.

powerUpRarityId.description: Opaque companion to powerUpValue. NOT a has-glyph flag: on a live account 4091 of 5495 glyphed lines report 0 here, so 0 does not mean 'no glyph' - test powerUpValue != 0 instead. Only 0 and 1 observed, and no line has a non-zero rarity with a zero glyph value; what the id distinguishes is not established.

scrollBalance.description: Mastery-scroll balance. ALWAYS carries all three rarities, defaulting to 0.
